scan_metadata.notes: Fresh shallow clone of default branch (depth 20); has_uncommitted_changes reflects the clone (false), not the author's working copy. Repository is a collection of QGIS 4 Processing scripts (Scripts/), a QGIS plugin (Plugins/metadata_manager), a tkinter desktop tool (Scripts/qgis_project_manager.py) and 65 Markdown documents. No web server or HTTP routes exist, so interface route detection is empty by design. Documentation (docs/), test fixtures, screenshots and docs/*/testing files were inventoried but not recorded as findings. Test and doc files containing example passwords (e.g. test_uri_parsing.py with password='p', docstring example password='s3cr3t' in qgis_project_manager.py) are fixtures/examples and were not recorded as secrets. SQL injection entries are low because the interpolated table/layer names come from the local user via the QGIS UI, not from a remote source. Personal author email appears in plugin metadata.txt (standard QGIS plugin metadata). The .gitignore excludes *.json, *.xml, *.jpg and many data formats, which may hide config files. The mqs4/.github/workflows/release-mapsplat.yml references a project that the README says moved to its own repo (stale).

gitignore_gaps: *.pem, *.key, credentials.json and similar credential file patterns are not listed (standard .env, .venv, venv exclusions are present)

findings: pyproject.toml has no runtime dependencies (empty list) and one dev dependency, pytest>=9.0.2 (unpinned lower bound, locked in uv.lock)
Scripts/qgis_project_manager.py requires psycopg2 (docstring says pip install psycopg2-binary) but there is no manifest for Scripts/ declaring it
Scripts and plugin rely on QGIS-bundled Python, qgis.core and osgeo (GDAL), which are not declared

proper_secret_handling_found.mechanism: getpass.getpass() interactive prompt for the plugins.qgis.org password
PostgreSQL password entered in a GUI field; supports authcfg (QGIS auth config id) and can strip user/password from project URIs

sql_injection_risk.reason: lines 638 and 664 build SELECT/UPDATE statements with an f-string table name (layer_name); the value comes from a QGIS dialog field, not from untrusted remote input; values are otherwise parameterized
line 791 builds ALTER TABLE [old] RENAME TO [new] with names from the user's selected layers/rename rules; local desktop use, no remote input
no string-built SQL found in db/manager.py or db/schema.py in the pattern scan

databases.credential_source: unclear (entered in tkinter GUI fields or parsed from QGIS project datasource URIs, which may embed user/password)

sql_injection_risk.reason: queries use psycopg2 parameters and psycopg2.sql Identifier composition (lines 487-547, 725-734)

what_this_app_can_do: Scans user-chosen directories for geospatial files (vector, raster, metadata files) and builds an inventory GeoPackage with extents; records the scanning user name and machine name.
Lets a user create and edit layer metadata (contacts, keywords, links) through a wizard and writes it to a local cache database and .qmd files.
Batch-renames vector layers and their files/tables with backup copies; converts vectors into GeoPackages; extracts styles from QGIS projects.
Reads QGIS project files, can connect to a PostgreSQL server with user-supplied credentials to read and update project content stored in a database table, and can export modified project XML.
Includes a command-line uploader that sends a plugin zip with username and password to plugins.qgis.org.

data_sources_touched.source: Local geospatial files and directories chosen by the user (scanned and renamed)
Inventory/metadata GeoPackage and SQLite cache databases
PostgreSQL database holding QGIS projects (qgis_project_manager.py, user-supplied host)
data_sources_touched.leaves_organization: unclear (depends on the host the user enters)

capability_summary.who_can_reach_it: Desktop tools run locally by the QGIS user; no network listener and no authentication layer of their own.
unauthorized_action_red_flags: Inventory records capture the OS user name and machine host name of whoever ran the scan.
qgis_project_manager.py parses and can display/test PostgreSQL credentials embedded in QGIS project datasource URIs.
plugin_upload.py transmits a username and password to plugins.qgis.org over HTTPS XML-RPC (author-supplied, interactive prompt).

top_findings: Local desktop QGIS tools: no routes, no hardcoded secrets or committed secret files
Low: f-string table names in SQL (inventory_processor.py:638/664, batchvectorrename.py:791), values come from local UI
qgis_project_manager.py handles PostgreSQL passwords from project URIs and a GUI field
Scripts/ requires psycopg2 but has no dependency manifest
